title: Status
summary: git status shows which files are new, changed, deleted or staged, so you know what the next commit will contain.

levels.title: What changed?
levels.briefing: git status compares three places: the last commit, the staging area and your folder. It lists staged changes, unstaged changes and untracked files separately.
levels.objective: One tracked file has changed since the last commit. Find it with git status and stage only that file. Leave scratch.txt untracked.

cheatsheet.description: List staged, changed and untracked files
The same, one line per file

hints: Look for the file listed as modified.
git add . would also stage scratch.txt. Name the file instead.
levels.successMessage: git status showed menu.txt as modified, so you staged exactly that file.

levels.title: A missing file
levels.objective: A tracked file was deleted. Stage the deletion.
hints: git status lists the file as deleted.
Staging a deleted file stages its removal.
levels.successMessage: Deletions are changes too, and they are staged the same way.

levels.title: Only what is staged
levels.objective: Some changes are staged and some are not. Commit only the staged ones.
hints: git status shows which change is already staged.
git commit only saves what is staged, so do not add anything else.
levels.successMessage: The unstaged change to b.txt is still waiting in your folder.

levels.title: A clean tree
levels.objective: Commit every change, including the new file, until git status says the working tree is clean.
hints: There is a modified file and an untracked file.
Run: git add ., then git commit -m "Save everything"
levels.successMessage: "Working tree clean" means everything in your folder matches the last commit.
